title: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence
slides: Apate sends AI agents to get scammed. What's the catch?
Agents pretend to be vulnerable to attract fraudsters.
Unlike honey pots, they extract actionable intelligence in real time.
You can now block scams before they reach your customers.
Test one scam scenario with your team this week.
thread_text:
1. The Trap That Bites Back

Apate uses AI agents that pose as easy targets. Fraudsters engage, but every move is logged and analyzed.

2. Bait That Thinks

These agents don't just wait—they actively lure scammers by mimicking vulnerable users. Real-time extraction turns the tables.

3. Beyond the Honeypot

Traditional traps only observe. Apate's agents extract actionable intelligence instantly, turning each scam attempt into a data point.

4. Block Before They Reach You

With live threat intelligence, you can stop scams before they ever hit your customers' inboxes.

5. Test Your Defenses Now

Pick one scam scenario and run a simulation with your team this week. If you haven't, start there.

Fraudsters can now be tricked into scamming an AI agent that logs every move.

Apate sends undercover agents posing as vulnerable users, pulling scammers into conversations they think are easy wins.

Unlike old honeypots that just watch, these agents extract usable fraud intelligence in real time. 🕵️

If you run content or a community, scam attempts hitting your audience can be flagged and stopped earlier. ⚡
